newsitem.title: USA: Democrats craft consumer-oriented bank proposals.
newsitem.headline: Democrats craft consumer-oriented bank proposals.

text.p: Democrats on the House Banking Committee met Wednesday to hammer out a strategy on bank reform that would bolster consumer protection provisions, staffers and lobbyists said.
The minority party lawmakers will also seek to delay a planned mark-up of bank reform legislation, currently scheduled for June 11, by one or more weeks, staffers said.
"There has not been enough time," one Democratic staffer said. "A new bill is coming out, the administration plan just came out, and there are a lot of things to be fine-tuned."
Under the Clinton plan, for example, banks selling insurance could be exempted by federal bank regulators from state insurance laws that applied to others selling insurance.

"Such a standard may prevent states from enacting or enforcing consumer safeguards," Consumers Union said earlier in the week. Without better protections, "financial modernization will benefit only special interests, not consumers," the publisher of Consumer Reports magazine warned.
Democrats were to meet with committee chairman Jim Leach, Republican of Iowa, Wednesday evening to air their concerns.
At their caucus, Democrats also discussed the effect of legislation on the the 1977 Community Reinvestment Act, which requires banks to make loans in poor neighborhoods.
Lawmakers decided to try to amend the bill to extend the reinvestment act to cover a diversified financial institution's non-bank activities.
Under such a proposal, a company that operated a bank, a securities firm and an insurance company might be required to make loans in poor areas based on its activity in all three businesses.
Currently, the act does not apply to activities conducted by separate affiliates of a bank holding company.
